assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframes intracellular organisation as liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent macromolecules, a genuinely new physical-chemical concept of molecular organisation that brings phase behaviour and thermodynamics into cell biology. Original, clear and enormously influential across biology, soft matter and disease research.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules and nucleoli as liquid condensates; Rosen provided the quantitative multivalency and phase-diagram framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence grammar and could be argued in, but three is a coherent core. Some credit overlap with earlier polymer and colloid physics remains.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely confirmed and growing fast, but debate continues over which condensates are truly phase-separated, functional relevance in vivo, and artefacts of overexpression. Recognition is timely; the conceptual core is stable even if specific cases are contested.
uncertainties: Biological function versus mere in vitro demixing remains debated for many condensates.
Fair allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not fully settled.
I am relying on my own memory of the literature and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly solution to nucleic-acid delivery: pH-dependent charge, nanoparticle formation and membrane fusion enabled siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines. The impact on medicine is very large and rests on lipid physical chemistry I know well.
assessment.attribution: Cullis group work on lipid polymorphism, ionizable lipids and rapid-mixing formulation is central; Hope and Madden were key to the formulation and early liposome technology. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan made significant lipid and clinical contributions, so allocation is genuinely contentious, and the mRNA vaccine prize in Medicine 2023 complicates framing.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale (patisiran, COVID-19 vaccines), so maturity is very high. Timing is right, with the risk that the Medicine recognition of mRNA is seen as having covered the topic.
uncertainties: Credit split among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved.
Whether the discovery reads as chemistry or as already honoured under Medicine 2023.
I did not verify specific patent or publication priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and funnel picture explains how proteins fold despite Levinthal's paradox, a unifying statistical-mechanical principle linking thermodynamics, kinetics and evolution. It is exactly the kind of reduction of messy biology to physical-chemical principles that I value, with lasting impact on folding and structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes introduced the spin-glass-inspired landscape; Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel and frustration framework; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations. Fersht provided key experimental mapping (phi-value analysis) and is a plausible alternative to Dill. The theory-versus-experiment split may need care.
assessment.maturity: Well established and now conceptually standard; AlphaFold-era recognition in 2024 may shift the perceived urgency of folding theory, but the landscape view remains foundational and mature.
uncertainties: Whether theory-only recognition is preferred over a combined theory and experiment prize with Fersht.
Overlap with the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction.
Precise priority among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Bryngelson.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduces a new pharmacological modality built on induced proximity, with strong chemical-biology originality and a growing clinical pipeline. Understanding of thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism adds a clean chemistry-biology story.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli, Gray and others advanced VHL ligands and degrader design. The eight-name credit list shows how crowded allocation is, with a three-person limit forcing hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but not yet complete, with approvals still pending for key degraders; recognition is somewhat early though the concept is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Clinical maturity not yet demonstrated by approved PROTAC drugs.
Allocation among many contributors is contested.
Details of priority between early PROTAC and glue work are from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids site-specifically, giving chemists control over protein composition in living systems. Broad, original and widely used tool with clear lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair strategy and first incorporation in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multiple codons and genome recoding; Lei Wang contributed early key work in Schultz lab and subsequent methods. Mehl and Yokoyama have respectable claims, so allocation is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in many labs; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is not fully clear.
Part of the impact is as an enabling tool rather than a conceptual discovery, which some members may weigh differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and DNA nanostructures show programmable self-assembly with nanometre precision, a concrete demonstration of design principles for molecular organisation from base-pairing thermodynamics. Conceptually elegant and widely applied.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's origami is the decisive contribution; Winfree contributed algorithmic self-assembly and tile theory; Yan advanced designed 2D/3D DNA nanostructures. Seeman, founder of the field, is not in the supplied credited names, which complicates fairness and I cannot resolve that from the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a field, but practical applications beyond demonstration remain limited, so some may see the chemistry impact as still developing.
uncertainties: Seeman's foundational role is absent from the credited names.
Real-world application impact is still modest.
Allocation among Rothemund, Winfree, Yan, Yin and Shih is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers, with soft lithography, defined how organic molecules organise at interfaces and gave control of surface chemistry, wetting and patterning. A foundational interfacial self-assembly concept with wide use in sensing, electronics and biology.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported thiol/disulfide monolayers on gold; Whitesides broadened the chemistry and invented soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority. Xia contributed to soft lithography.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and confirmed, arguably late rather than premature. Concern is whether it is seen as a past-peak topic.
uncertainties: Priority with Sagiv for monolayer formation.
Whether the soft lithography portion belongs with the same prize.
Memory-based assessment of precise dates and roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages shows how coordination thermodynamics yields complex defined architectures, with host-guest chemistry, confined catalysis and encapsulation. Strong supramolecular concept fitting a physical-chemical view of self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Fujita's cages and Raymond's tetrahedral and related hosts are the main early contributors; Nitschke extended to subcomponent self-assembly and complex structures; Stang's molecular architecture work is also major. Choosing three omits genuinely important people.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation and diverse applications; timing is fair, though the field overlaps with 2016 supramolecular and 1987 host-guest prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with previous supramolecular prizes.
Allocation among Fujita, Raymond, Stang, Nitschke and Ward.
Concrete applications beyond showcase systems are still emerging.
